title: A piece can take the room a row has left over
goal: Inside a stack, one piece can be told to take whatever room is left along the direction the stack runs, so the search field in the middle of a nav bar grows with the bar and a button spans the width of a toolbar. Today every piece in a stack keeps the size it was drawn at along that direction and only the gap between them can change.
notes: GroupFlow.stacked() takes `along` straight from item.box on the flow axis and never reads that axis' placement rule, so today there is nothing to fill with. The cross axis already does this through span(size:start:extent:rule:) with .stretch, so the naming to reuse is there. The row that has to grow the choice is the 'owned by the flow' row in PlacementInspector.swift, which currently only says the stack decides it; childCaption is where the one line about a hugging stack goes. The pending task a-row-can-push-its-contents-to-its-two-ends edits the same function for the space between case: whichever lands first, the second reads it rather than re-deciding how leftover room is worked out. Watch the surface piece (stretch both ways), which is not one of the things being arranged and must not join the sharing.
acceptance: On the axis a stack runs along, a piece is offered Fill as well as the sentence saying the stack decides where it sits, and picking it makes that piece take the room left after the other pieces, the gaps and the room at the edges have taken theirs
Two pieces set to Fill share what is left equally, and a piece set to Fill is never squeezed below nothing
A stack that closes around its contents has no room left over, so Fill is not offered there and one line says why rather than a dead menu item
Turning Fill off gives the piece back the size it had before

Ships behind next-auto-layout. To see it: open Photonz Next, draw three rectangles in a row, group them, set the group to Stack and give it a width of 800, pick the middle rectangle and set its horizontal rule to Fill, then drag the group wider and watch only the middle one grow
Tests in PhotonzCore cover one filler, two fillers, both directions, room at the edges and the hugging case, written before any app code
Anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task

log.note: Adversarial review before building. (1) Fill cannot reuse Stretch on the flow axis: stretch both ways already means 'surface behind the rest', and a search field that fills a nav bar across AND fills its height down would silently become the surface. So Fill is its own thing, not a sixth placement value. (2) Fill is NOT a placement at all: it is a flow property, so it rides on the layer as one optional (FlowFill) rather than adding a case to two public enums, PlacementSpan, every placement menu and LayerScaling. Flipping a stack from row to column then keeps meaning 'take the room the flow has left', which a horizontal .fill would not. (3) Fill collides with Spread (space-between): both claim the leftover. Rule: a filler wins and the others sit the typed gap apart, which is what flexbox does. The alternative leaves every gap at nought and looks broken. (4) Cut: Fill is not offered on the group's Contents row. 'Everything inside fills' is equal columns, which is what a grid already is. (5) A filler takes the leftover INSTEAD of its own size (Figma's reading), not its size plus a share, which is what 'the search field grows with the bar' means. (6) A column stack filling a text layer has to pass fillingHeight, or the text ignores the height it is handed.

Built. Core: FlowFill on Layer (one optional, so a document from before decodes untouched), GroupFlow.alongTheFlow works out each piece's length along the flow, GroupLayout.hasRoomAlongTheFlow is now the one question both spreading and filling ask, PlacementEditing gains canFill / fillTitle / noRoomToFill, PhotonzDocument.setFillsTheFlow records the size on the way in and hands it back on the way out. App: the flow-owned row in PlacementInspector became a two-answer menu. 27 new tests in GroupFillTests, whole suite 3461 green.

Adversarial review on the real app, driven by Scripts/playtest/fill-the-flow-walk.json against the probe (Screen Recording granted, so the pictures are real captures). Two things were clumsy and both are fixed: (1) the answer read plain 'Fill' while the Colour section three rows down also says Fill, in the same panel at the same time, so it now names the flow: 'Fill the row' / 'Fill the stack'. (2) The W field stayed typeable while the stack owned the number, so a typed width was silently put back on the next pass; it is now a number to read with a tip naming the two controls that do change it. Two rough edges filed rather than fixed: the old cross-axis Stretch has the same dead-field wart, and there is no menu item or key for filling.

One piece in a stack can take the room the stack has left along the way it runs. Model: FlowFill on Layer plus GroupFlow.alongTheFlow; offer: PlacementEditing.canFill over GroupLayout.hasRoomAlongTheFlow, which couldSpread now reads too; edit: PhotonzDocument.setFillsTheFlow, which remembers the size and hands it back. The flow-owned row in PlacementInspector became a two-answer menu reading 'Fill the row' / 'Fill the stack'. Verified by 27 new tests in GroupFillTests (whole suite 3461 green) and by driving the probe app with Scripts/playtest/fill-the-flow-walk.json, with real screen captures. Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-05-fill-the-flow.json.
